name: Unterperfuss
kurzbeschreibung: Tiniest municipality in the Innsbruck-Land district, with a rural charm and views of the Stubaier Alpen.
beschreibung:
Unterperfuss lies at an altitude of 596 metres above sea level in the district of Innsbruck-Land and, with around 200 inhabitants, is the smallest municipality in this district. The village is located at the entrance to the Sellraintal, only about 15 kilometres west of the provincial capital Innsbruck, and together with its neighbouring village Oberperfuss forms a small district of its own. Despite its proximity to the city, Unterperfuss retains its distinctly rural character, which can already be seen in the manageable number of farms and residential buildings.

The location at the foot of the Stubaier Alpen shapes the appearance of the village: from Unterperfuss, the view extends far across the Inntal, and especially the opposite Nordkette with its rugged rock faces is impressive on a clear day. The surrounding area invites walks and hikes, with the tranquillity here noticeably more palpable than in the region's well-known tourist resorts. Agricultural land and meadows define the scene around the village, and anyone seeking silence will find it here among fields, old farmsteads and the wide valley floor.

Culturally, Unterperfuss is closely connected with the parish of Oberperfuss, to which the village belongs ecclesiastically. The proximity to Innsbruck also makes the municipality a quiet place to live, from which both the city and the ski areas of the Stubaier Alpen and Kühtai are easily reachable – a location that is quite rare in the district of Innsbruck-Land.
